name: If–Then Start Protocol
shortExplanation: Connect one recognizable cue to one concrete first action.
intendedProblem: Delayed initiation, forgetting, or distraction at a predictable moment.
mayHelpWhen: The same situation repeatedly precedes avoidance.
The first action can be made concrete and small.
unsuitableWhen: The obstacle is lack of skill or resources rather than initiation.

evidence.limitation: Effects vary by goal, population, and the quality of the plan. A cue-action plan does not remove structural barriers.
evidence.rationale: Implementation-intention research supports specific if–then plans for goal pursuit.

setupQuestions: What situation reliably occurs before the action?
What is the smallest observable first action?

steps.title: Name the cue
steps.instruction: Choose a situation that is likely to occur and easy to recognize.

steps.title: Name the first action
steps.instruction: Define one action that can begin in under two minutes.

steps.title: Write the link
steps.instruction: Use the form: When X occurs, I will do Y.

minimumVersion: Perform only the first observable action.
focusRule: Optionally protect the first 20–45 minutes from selected distracting apps.
stopConditions: The action is repeatedly impossible in that context.

name: Obstacle Plan
shortExplanation: Contrast the desired outcome with the most likely internal obstacle, then prepare a response.
intendedProblem: Repeated failure caused by a predictable internal obstacle.
mayHelpWhen: The user can name a likely obstacle rather than only a vague lack of motivation.
unsuitableWhen: The problem is primarily external and cannot be changed by a personal response plan.

evidence.limitation: Average effects are modest and context-dependent; publication bias has been discussed in the literature.
evidence.rationale: Mental contrasting with implementation intentions has controlled and meta-analytic support.

inspiration: Mental contrasting with implementation intentions / WOOP research
setupQuestions: What outcome matters?
What internal obstacle is most likely?
What response is realistic when it appears?

steps.title: Outcome
steps.instruction: Describe the observable result you want.

steps.title: Obstacle
steps.instruction: Name the most likely internal barrier.

steps.title: Response
steps.instruction: Write an if–then response to that barrier.

minimumVersion: Name one obstacle and one response.
stopConditions: The identified obstacle is consistently wrong.

name: Context Anchor
shortExplanation: Repeat a small behavior in a stable context and observe whether it becomes easier to initiate.
intendedProblem: Inconsistent repetition caused by changing cues and schedules.
mayHelpWhen: A stable place, preceding action, or time window exists.
unsuitableWhen: The user has no recurring context or the behavior must vary constantly.

evidence.limitation: Habit-formation time varies widely; there is no universal 21- or 66-day rule.
evidence.rationale: Stable contextual repetition is associated with growing automaticity.

inspiration: Habit automaticity research — Lally et al.
setupQuestions: Which context is genuinely stable?
What version of the behavior is repeatable there?

steps.title: Choose context
steps.instruction: Select a recurring cue such as after breakfast or arriving at the library.

steps.title: Repeat one behavior
steps.instruction: Keep the first action consistent in that context.

steps.title: Rate automaticity
steps.instruction: Notice whether starting requires less conscious effort over time.

minimumVersion: Do the first 60 seconds in the chosen context.
stopConditions: The context is not stable enough to be useful.

name: Progress Mirror
shortExplanation: Collect the smallest useful evidence of progress and review the trend instead of protecting a meaningless streak.
intendedProblem: Poor feedback about whether effort is producing useful progress.
mayHelpWhen: A meaningful output or behavior can be counted or rated.
unsuitableWhen: The metric would encourage harmful or obsessive tracking.

evidence.limitation: Monitoring helps most when the metric is relevant and feedback is actually reviewed.

setupQuestions: What is the smallest meaningful evidence?
How often is a review useful?

steps.title: Choose evidence
steps.instruction: Pick one metric tied to the desired outcome.

steps.title: Log honestly
steps.instruction: Record the result without filling gaps to preserve a streak.

steps.title: Review the trend
steps.instruction: Use the review to continue, simplify, modify, or stop.

stopConditions: The metric is not related to the outcome.
Tracking creates more burden than information.
sourceLabels: Harkin et al. — monitoring goal progress

name: Temptation Pairing
shortExplanation: Pair an immediately enjoyable activity with a valuable delayed-reward behavior when the two are compatible.
intendedProblem: A useful behavior consistently loses to a more immediately rewarding option.
mayHelpWhen: The enjoyable activity does not interfere with performance or safety.
unsuitableWhen: The pairing reduces learning, attention, exercise safety, or task quality.

evidence.limitation: Evidence is domain-specific and should not be generalized to every behavior.
evidence.rationale: Temptation bundling has field-experimental support, particularly in exercise settings.

inspiration: Temptation bundling research — Milkman, Minson & Volpp
setupQuestions: What enjoyable activity is genuinely tempting?
Can it coexist with the target behavior without degrading it?

steps.title: Choose the valuable action
steps.instruction: Name the delayed-reward behavior.

steps.title: Choose the temptation
steps.instruction: Pick an enjoyable activity reserved for compatible use.

steps.title: Test compatibility
steps.instruction: Stop the pairing if output or safety declines.

minimumVersion: Use the pairing for the first ten minutes.
stopConditions: The pairing distracts from the target behavior.

name: Fresh Start & Recovery
shortExplanation: Use a meaningful boundary to begin, then treat misses as diagnostic information rather than moral failure.
intendedProblem: Difficulty restarting after disruption or a missed day.
mayHelpWhen: A transition or chosen boundary can support a clear restart.
unsuitableWhen: Waiting for a landmark would unnecessarily delay urgent action.

evidence.limitation: Temporal landmarks can increase initiation, but effects are not guaranteed and do not replace practical planning.
evidence.rationale: Research on temporal landmarks supports a fresh-start effect in some contexts.

setupQuestions: What boundary is meaningful but not unnecessarily far away?
What actually caused the previous miss?

steps.title: Choose the restart
steps.instruction: Use today, Monday, return from travel, or another meaningful boundary.

steps.title: Diagnose the miss
steps.instruction: Classify the failure: ability, opportunity, motivation, task size, timing, or unrealistic rule.

steps.title: Change one thing
steps.instruction: Modify the protocol based on the diagnosis.

minimumVersion: Restart with the smallest version today.
stopConditions: The landmark is being used to procrastinate.

name: Attention Residue Guard
shortExplanation: Close one task cleanly before a protected focus block, capture stray thoughts, and leave a restart note.
intendedProblem: Task switching and digital interruptions during cognitively demanding work.
mayHelpWhen: The work benefits from sustained attention.
unsuitableWhen: The role requires continuous urgent responsiveness.

evidence.limitation: The complete protocol is an engineered application; evidence more directly supports the underlying attention-residue and interruption findings.
evidence.rationale: Task-switching research indicates attention can remain on unfinished prior work.

inspiration: Attention-residue research — Leroy; Deep Work inspired implementation
setupQuestions: What unfinished thought needs capturing?
Which interruptions are realistically suppressible?

steps.title: Clear residue
steps.instruction: Write unfinished thoughts from the prior task.

steps.title: Protect the block
steps.instruction: Select distracting apps to restrict for the planned duration.

steps.title: Leave a restart note
steps.instruction: End with one sentence describing the next action.

minimumVersion: Capture one unfinished thought and focus for 15 minutes.
focusRule: Block selected distracting apps during the protected block.

name: Autonomy Check
shortExplanation: Check whether a goal is personally chosen, appropriately challenging, and supported by useful relationships.
intendedProblem: Persistence problems where the goal feels imposed, punishing, or disconnected from personal reasons.
mayHelpWhen: The user is unsure why they are pursuing the goal.
unsuitableWhen: The immediate issue is a simple scheduling or knowledge gap.

evidence.limitation: Self-determination theory is broad; specific Methodra interface prompts are conservative applications, not independently validated treatments.
evidence.rationale: Self-determination research emphasizes autonomy, competence, and relatedness.

setupQuestions: Would I choose this goal without external pressure?
Is the difficulty challenging but learnable?
Who can provide useful support?

steps.title: Check choice
steps.instruction: Write the personal reason, or acknowledge that the goal is externally constrained.

steps.title: Check competence
steps.instruction: Reduce difficulty if the next action is currently impossible.

steps.title: Check support
steps.instruction: Name one useful source of feedback or help.

minimumVersion: Write one personally meaningful reason or decide to reconsider the goal.
stopConditions: The goal is persistently unwanted and optional.

name: Recall Protocol
shortExplanation: Replace passive review with retrieval attempts, delayed revisits, and corrective feedback.
intendedProblem: Study time that feels productive but produces weak recall.
mayHelpWhen: The goal involves learning retrievable knowledge or procedures.
unsuitableWhen: The task is primarily exploratory reading with no current retrieval goal.

evidence.limitation: Retrieval practice is powerful for learning, but prompt quality, feedback, spacing, and material type still matter.
evidence.rationale: Retrieval-practice and distributed-learning research has substantial experimental support.

inspiration: Retrieval practice research; Make It Stick as an accessible synthesis
setupQuestions: What should be retrievable without notes?
When will the next retrieval attempt occur?

steps.title: Close the source
steps.instruction: Attempt one question or explanation from memory.

steps.title: Check feedback
steps.instruction: Compare the attempt with a reliable source and correct errors.

steps.title: Schedule another retrieval
steps.instruction: Revisit after a delay instead of immediately rereading.

minimumVersion: Answer one question from memory before looking.
focusRule: Optionally protect the retrieval block from distracting apps.
stopConditions: Questions do not match the material being learned.
sourceLabels: Brown, Roediger & McDaniel — Make It Stick inspiration

name: Voluntary Commitment
shortExplanation: Preselect a reversible restriction that protects a decision you already want to make.
intendedProblem: Predictable temptation during a planned work period.
mayHelpWhen: The user explicitly wants extra friction against a known distraction.
unsuitableWhen: Restriction could interfere with safety, caregiving, accessibility, or essential communication.

evidence.limitation: Commitment-device evidence varies by domain. Methodra uses no financial punishment and never claims restrictions are impossible to bypass.
evidence.rationale: Commitment devices have controlled evidence in several behavioral domains.

setupQuestions: Which apps are genuinely distracting?
What emergency path must remain available?

steps.title: Choose restrictions
steps.instruction: Select only apps you want Methodra to add friction to.

steps.title: Set the window
steps.instruction: Choose a clear start, duration, and optional daily budget.

steps.title: Keep an exit
steps.instruction: Emergency exit remains available with a short reason for later review.

focusRule: Use Methodra focus protection with a deliberate emergency exit.
stopConditions: The permission burden exceeds the benefit.
